previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and tremulousness after taking sertraline, tramadol, and Zofran. There was concern for possible serotonin syndrome, though toxicology deemed it unlikely. She was treated with IV fluids, Ativan, and Reglan while holding tramadol, Zofran, and sertraline. Her symptoms resolved, and she was advanced to a regular diet. Her diabetes was stabilized with insulin, and she completed her H. pylori antibiotic course. Chronic back pain management was transitioned from opioids to lidocaine patch, tizanidine, and Tylenol. Psychiatry recommended possible SSRI restart outpatient with close follow-up. She was discharged home with improved condition and multiple follow-up appointments arranged.
